subject: SIG / CAIQ: annotated isolation legend + attacker-scenarios appendix
messages:
From: Jane Palmer <jane.palmer@acerocloud.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: AceroCloud Security <security@acerocloud.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SIG / CAIQ - isolation legend + attacker-scenarios appendix request

Kimberly —

Thanks for the quick turn so far on the CAIQ. Our assessment team ran through the questionnaire and flagged a few follow-ups where we need an "annotated isolation legend" and a short appendix that walks through plausible attacker scenarios against Dedicated / Private deployments. Specifically we need:

- A one-page legend describing the symbols/labels used on your network diagrams (control plane, data plane, sidecar, airlocks, KMS boundary, customer-managed VPC connectors).
- 2–3 attacker scenarios (low/medium/high) describing how a bad actor could attempt lateral movement and how your controls mitigate each step.
- A mapping table that points each scenario back to CAIQ/SIG control IDs where applicable.

Can you confirm if you can deliver a marked-up topology (SVG or PDF) plus the attacker-scenarios workbook? Our reviewers prefer separate logical diagrams (service-level) and provider-level VPC sketches.

Attached: SIG-CAIQ_questionnaire_v1.pdf (annotated questions).

Target: internal review next Tuesday (2026-11-17). Is that feasible?

Thanks,
Jane
Jane Palmer
Senior Security Engineer — AceroCloud
security@acerocloud.com

Attachments: SIG-CAIQ_questionnaire_v1.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Jane Palmer <jane.palmer@acerocloud.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SIG / CAIQ - isolation legend + attacker-scenarios appendix request

Jane —

Acknowledged, thanks for the clear ask. We can produce:

1) An annotated legend PDF (single page) that maps our diagram symbology to CAIQ/SIG control families.
2) Two diagram flavors: logical service map (shows inference runtime components and sidecars) and provider/VPC sketch (shows subnets, route tables, NAT/egress, and customer-managed VPNs).
3) An attacker-scenarios workbook (xlsx) with step-by-step attack trees and the corresponding mitigations and evidence pointers (logs, ACLs, KMS attestations).

Vivek and Marissa are looped in to pull the diagrams and the evidence pointers. Can you confirm whether you need network-level packet-capture examples or just configuration artifacts (ACLs, route tables, KMS key IDs)? Also, do you want the mapping to reference CAIQ question IDs or SIG control names? We can do either, but CAIQ question IDs are easiest for auditors to cross-reference.

We plan an initial delivery by Monday EOD (2026-11-16) and a final package by Tuesday morning to hit your review window; will that align with your reviewers?

Best,

Kimberly Park
Director, Security Architecture
Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
(415) 555-0198

Attachments: isolation_legend_draft.svg (SVG, draft)

---

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jane Palmer <jane.palmer@acerocloud.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SIG / CAIQ - isolation legend + attacker-scenarios appendix request

Kimberly / Marissa —

I attached a draft of the diagram legend (isolation_legend_draft.svg) and a brief notes sheet in the drive link. High-level notes for the workbook:

- Scenario A (Low): misconfigured customer-managed VPC peering allows discovery. Mitigation: VPC route table policy + tenant egress guards; evidence = route table exports, flow logs sample (redacted).
- Scenario B (Medium): credential compromise of a sidecar that has narrow KMS access. Mitigation: short-lived sidecar credentials, signed attestation, strict IAM role scoping; evidence = KMS key policy snapshot, sidecar identity docs.
- Scenario C (High): supply-chain compromise on a model artifact leading to model poisoning and data exfiltration. Mitigation: model signing, content-addressed storage, network egress airlocks; evidence = sigchain hash, airlock ACLs.

Two clarifications for Acero:
1) When you say "provider-level VPC sketches" do you want annotated cloud console screenshots or neutral SVGs with CIDR/route callouts? Neutral SVGs are faster and avoid sharing console images.
2) For mapping to SIG/CAIQ, we will include both the control name and the CAIQ question ID in the workbook (two columns).

I can assemble the workbook template today and populate A/B/C scenarios with mitigation references. Marissa can pull the configuration snapshots for the evidence pointers.

Vivek
Principal Architect, Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments: isolation_legend_draft.svg (SVG, 78KB)

From: Jane Palmer <jane.palmer@acerocloud.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: AceroCloud Security <security@acerocloud.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SIG / CAIQ - isolation legend + attacker-scenarios appendix request

Kimberly / Vivek / Marissa —

This looks great — neutral SVGs are preferred. For evidence, configuration artifacts (ACLs, route table dumps, KMS key IDs) are sufficient; we do not need PCAPs at this stage. Please include CAIQ IDs where available (that will speed up the auditor review).

Timeline: Monday EOD (2026-11-16) for an initial package is fine; our reviewers will triage and send any targeted follow-ups. If you can include a one-slide summary (PDF) that lists the three scenarios and the primary mitigations, that will help execs.

I'll allocate a reviewer for Tuesday morning. Thanks for moving quickly.

—Jane
